steps: Uncrate & unpack
Remove the crating top and supports and the plastic cover, then take the brick pack out of the firebox. Fit the firebricks only once the stove is in its final location and the chimney is installed.
A/C adapter & battery box
Take the A/C adapter from inside the unit, plug its barrel plug into the control board, then plug the adapter into a wall outlet. Fit the optional battery box per its own instructions.
Flue thermocouple guard
Remove the guard from inside the flue collar and the cardboard holding the flue gas agitator, then refit the guard with all three ends in place. Never operate with the agitator removed.
Floor protector
Combustible floors need continuous non-combustible ember protection: USA 16" front and 8" to the sides of the fuel loading door opening; Canada 18" on the firing side and 8" on the other sides.

USA16" (406 mm) front · 8" (203 mm) to the sides of the fuel loading door opening
USA minimum33"(838mm) wide · 34 3/8" overall depth
Canada18" (457 mm) firing side · 8" (203 mm) other sides
Canada minimum43 3/4"(1.11m) wide · 45 1/8"(1.15 m) overall depth

USA: protection is also required under the chimney connector, plus 2" (51 mm) beyond each side, with any horizontal venting. Don't obstruct the space beneath the heater.

Note: for US floor protection, the rating label on p. 3 gives 16 inches front, 5 inches side and 0 inches back; p. 17 gives 8" (203 mm) to the sides of the fuel loading door opening, and its drawing shows a 3" (75mm) dimension the text doesn't label.
Position & mark

Set the stove (pedestal or leg kit attached) and floor protection to the clearances. Plumb-bob from the flue centre to mark the ceiling and roof holes, check joists and rafters, then reconfirm clearances.
Chimney

UL-103 HT (USA) or ULC-S629 (Canada) listed, or a lined masonry chimney for solid fuel; 6" flue, minimum system height 15 feet. Install it per the chimney maker's directions from the ceiling through to the rain cap.
Chimney connector
Crimped end into the stove collar, fixed with three screws; crimped ends down and 3 sheet metal screws at every joint. Never through an attic, roof space, closet, floor or ceiling.

Single wall: as short and straight as possible, six inch diameter, 24 gauge black pipe, clean and in new condition. Slip the crimped edge inside the stove collar and secure it with three screws through the holes provided. Crimped or male ends point down so liquid creosote or condensation runs back into the stove; secure every joint and collar with 3 sheet metal screws. Join to the chimney with the manufacturer's approved adapter (a slip section helps).

Double wall: use a listed double-wall connector, installed to the chimney/connector maker's requirements. For close clearances, use a listed double-wall connector.

An offset is allowed if all sections of listed connector, offset elbows and chimney are screwed together with at least three sheet metal screws per joint and the chimney is supported by the maker's listed offset support. For an up-and-out installation, the drawing on p. 21 calls for a 12" [300mm] minimum first section of pipe; give it as much vertical length as possible, as the unit may be harder to start.

Through a combustible wall (NFPA 211, pp. 23-24)

System A12 in. (305mm) to combustibles · 3.5 in. brick wall, 5/8 in. fireclay liner
System B9 in. (229mm) · listed solid-insulated chimney length, 1 in. insulation
System C6 in. (152mm) · 24 gauge ventilated thimble, two 1 in. air channels, glass fiber insulation
System D2 in. (51mm) · listed chimney length 2 in. larger than the connector, 12 in. min. length

Maintain the vapour barrier wherever the chimney penetrates to the exterior. Otherwise follow CAN/CSA-B365 or NFPA 211.
Combustion air

Room air enters through the ash box enclosure; for outside air, run 4" metal venting through the floor to the 4" OAIR adapter, or fit a 4" wall air intake behind. Residential outside air means securing the stove to the structure.
Mobile home requirements
Listed double-wall connector and ULC-S629 or UL-103HT chimney, outside air, legs anchored with 1/4-20 x 2" lag screws. Never in a sleeping room; keep the floor, walls and roof structurally sound.
Install the firebricks
Rear wall first, then each side wall, then the floor and front row. One brick is left over as a spare.

A8 7/8" x 4 3/8" x 1 1/4"
B8 7/8" x 2 1/8" x 1 1/4"
C5 3/4" x 4 3/8" x 1 1/4"
D4 3/8" x 3 1/4" x 1 1/4"
E7" x 3 1/4" x 1 1/4"
F4 1/4" x 2 1/8" x 1 1/4"
  1. Rear wall: stand an A brick vertically behind the brick-rail tab and slide it toward the centre; slide a second A under the tab. Repeat for the other rear A bricks.
  2. Side wall: an A against the side wall and the rear brick, another A beside it, then a narrow B.
  3. Set a D on top of the A bricks and slide it back so it tucks in behind the brick rail.
  4. Slide an E under the side-wall brick-rail tab, resting on the three side bricks. Repeat steps 2-4 on the other side.
  5. Floor: two A bricks, plus a third A against the rear wall.
  6. Place the C beside the ash dump, against the left side wall and the A directly behind the ash dump.
  7. Front row: a short narrow F at the front right, a longer B in the centre, then the last F at the front left. A gap behind the ash dump is expected.

One brick is left over as a spare. The layout is shown in Figures 20-28 (pp. 26-28).

light.title: Lighting a fire
light.html:
Never use gasoline, lantern fuel, kerosene, charcoal lighter fluid or any similar liquid to start or "freshen up" a fire. Keep all such liquids well away from the stove while it's in use.

  1. Move the air control, under the ash lip, to High: all the way to the left. Open the door.
  2. Put crumpled newspaper in the centre of the stove and crisscross several pieces of small, dry kindling over it. Add a few pieces of large kindling on top.
  3. Light the paper. Leave the door open about 1/2" to 1" until the kindling is fully in flame. Never leave the stove unattended with the door open.
  4. Once the kindling is fully engulfed, add a few small pieces of wood and close the door.
  5. When there's a good bed of coals and the wood has charred, begin normal operation. From then on, keep the door closed: the stove isn't designed for open-door burning.

Your first 2-3 fires

The paint finish bakes on during the first few fires and can give off smoke and fumes. Open all windows and doors. Bring the stove slowly up to a medium burn for about 45 minutes, then a high burn for another 45-60 minutes. Follow the Stove Bright (Forrest Paint) sheet that came with your stove.

Pacific Energy strongly recommends smoke and carbon monoxide detectors near the stove. They may go off more often while the paint cures. Don't disconnect them.

air.title: Using the air control
air.html:
The air control sits under the ash lip. Facing the stove, move it right for Low and left for High; the middle is roughly Medium. Any position in between works for the burn rate and heat you want.

  • Low: for overnight or extended burns.
  • High: to light, and to char fresh wood after you reload. Run it on High for about 10-15 minutes, or until the wood is fully charred.

The right setting depends on your wood, the outside temperature, your chimney and the weather. You'll learn it with practice.

Don't over-fire. Don't run on High for long periods. A glowing red top or vent pipe means the stove is over-firing, which can permanently damage the stove and chimney and may void the warranty. An uncontrollable burn or glowing red parts mean too much draft; smoke leaking out at the stove or pipe joints means too little.

The factory-set minimum burn rate must not be altered. Federal regulations prohibit it.

With the optional blower

With the air control on Low, run the blower on Low. Between Low and High, use any blower speed. With the rocker switch on the fan housing set to Auto, the fan comes on as the stove heats up and shuts off after it cools. On Man, it runs until you turn it off.

reload.title: Reloading & overnight burns
reload.html:
To add wood

  1. Move the air control to High and give the fire time to brighten.
  2. Open the door slowly. That keeps smoke from coming out and prevents back puffing.
  3. Load dry wood parallel to the stove front, placed so air can flow between the logs. Mixed shapes and sizes are fine.
  4. Burn on High for about 10-15 minutes, until the wood is fully charred, then set the air where you want it.

Small loads burn cleanest: two or three logs at a time, or 1/4 to 1/2 of a full load, with the air fairly wide open for the first 10 to 30 minutes.

For an overnight burn

Use unsplit logs. Char the wood completely on the maximum setting, then slowly turn the air control to Low. Don't try to burn overnight with green or wet wood.

Restarting in the morning

  1. Open the door and rake the hot embers toward the front. Add a couple of dry, split logs on top and close the door.
  2. Set the air control to High. The logs should start burning within a few minutes.
  3. Once the wood has charred, reset the air control where you want it.
Note: the manual gives the maximum log length as 17 inches on p. 3 and up to 18" on p. 7. The ideal length is 16 inches.
Maker's website: Log Size (Max) 18″.

wood.title: What wood to burn
wood.html:
Burn natural wood only. Air-dried, seasoned hardwood gives higher efficiency and lower emissions than softwood or green wood. Season wood for six months or more, and store it under cover, away from open flame or heat.

Wet wood smoulders, makes lots of smoke and creosote, gives little heat and tends to go out. It can cut heat output by up to 25%.

Never burn

  • Wet, green or unseasoned wood, salt-water wood, treated wood or railroad ties
  • Garbage, lawn clippings, yard waste, manure or animal remains
  • Coal, charcoal, solvents, paints, thinners, petroleum or asphalt products
  • Anything with rubber, plastic or asbestos; construction or demolition debris
  • Paper products, cardboard, plywood or particleboard

Salt-water wood and garbage contain chlorides that quickly destroy metal and void the warranty. Fire starters made from paper, cardboard, sawdust or wax are fine for lighting. Never barbecue in the stove. If you feel you must burn wet or unseasoned wood, the manual says to keep the air open enough for a strong fire and fairly high chimney temperatures.

Test your wood

Put a large piece on a good bed of coals. Dry wood burns on more than one side within one minute. Damp wood turns black and lights within three minutes. If it sizzles, hisses and blackens without lighting in five minutes, it's soaked: don't burn it. A moisture meter can confirm.

ash.title: Removing ashes
ash.html:
Remove ashes only when the stove is cold. When ash is 3" to 4" deep and the fire has burned down and cooled, take out the excess. Leave about 1" of ash on the firebox bottom to help keep a hot charcoal bed.

Ash chute (ash lip)

Pull the ash pan out about 2", sweep ash from the ash lip into the chute on its right side, then close the ash pan.

Ash dump (firebox)

  1. The handle is under the ash lip on the left. Pull it out 1/2" and turn it clockwise to unlock the ash dump.
  2. Hold the handle open and pull ashes into the opening. Leave large embers; they still have heat value.
  3. Release the handle and push it in to lock. Check that the ash dump door is properly engaged, then fill the cavity with the remaining ash, level with the firebox floor.
  4. Lift out the ash pan, empty it into a metal container, and seat it back properly.
Never burn with the ash dump door open. Keep it closed whenever the stove is burning.

Store ashes in a metal container with a tight-fitting lid, on a non-combustible floor or the ground, well away from combustibles. Keep it closed until the cinders are thoroughly cool, and put no other waste in it.

glass.title: Glass & door gasket
glass.html:
Clean darkened glass with fireplace glass cleaner, only when the stove is cold. Never scrape it with anything that could scratch it, and don't use abrasive cleaners.

Hot glass will cause burns. Don't touch the glass until it has cooled, and never let children touch it.

What the deposit tells you

A light brown, dusty film that wipes off easily usually means good combustion, dry wood and fairly clean pipes and chimney. A black, greasy deposit that's hard to remove comes from wet or green wood and burning too slowly, and it's building up at least as fast in your chimney.

Protect the glass

  • Don't slam the door or hit the glass, and make sure no logs stick out when you close it.
  • If the glass cracks or breaks, replace it before you use the stove. Use only 10-1/2" x 16-1/2" x 5 mm ceramic glass from your dealer.

Door gasket

The door seal is 7/8" medium-density fiberglass rope and needs only light pressure to seal. Check it weekly for sagging, placement and damage, and replace it with the kit from your Pacific Energy dealer when needed. Dirty glass can also mean a leaking gasket or a door latch that needs checking.

chimney.title: Chimney, creosote & chimney fires
chimney.html:
Slow fires make tar and vapours that condense in a cool chimney as creosote, and creosote burns extremely hot. Some is inevitable; regular inspection and cleaning is the answer.

  • Inspect the chimney connector and chimney at least once every two months in the heating season. Remove creosote once it's 3 mm or more.
  • Until you know your stove, check for creosote daily. Mild weather may need weekly cleaning; monthly is usually enough in the coldest months.
  • To clean, disconnect the chimney connector from the stove. Remove the baffle only if that isn't possible.

Signs of a chimney fire

Flames and sparks shooting out of the top of the chimney, a roaring sound, or the chimney vibrating.

If it happens

  1. Get ready to evacuate. Everyone should know the plan and the meeting place outside.
  2. Close the air inlet on the stove.
  3. Call the fire department. Keep a fire extinguisher handy.
  4. Before the next fire, have the chimney cleaned and checked for stress and cracks. Check combustibles around the chimney and the roof too.
Pacific Energy strongly recommends a chimney inspection by an NFI, CSIA, WETT or APC certified professional.

maint.title: Maintenance checks
maint.html:
Check these parts for cracks, heavy corrosion, burned-out sections and excessive warping. If you find damage, contact your dealer: running the stove with broken parts can damage other parts and may void your warranty.

WeeklyFirebrick (cracking); door gasket (sagging, placement, damage)
MonthlyBrick rail tabs and rails; air riser tube at the back of the firebox; back of the airwash chamber; baffle locking pin; boost openings
At chimney cleaningTop baffle board/blanket; baffle and tubes; top heat shield and bolts; baffle gasket; brick rails
At least every six monthsVacuum the blower's grill openings at the back and bottom of its casing
  • Some baffle warping is normal, up to 1/4". Replace it if it's warped more, cracked or broken.
  • Keep the boost air area at the front of the firebox clear of ash buildup.
  • Replace broken or missing firebricks. Build fires directly on the bricks, never on a grate or andirons.
  • Use only materials supplied by the manufacturer for maintenance and replacements.
Never run the stove with the baffle, tubes, insulation or flue gas agitator removed.

power.title: Power, batteries & status lights
power.html:
The stove's control board runs from an A/C adapter plugged into a wall outlet.

In a power outage

Until power is back, the stove still runs within safe and certified limits using the manual air control at the front. With the optional battery box, it stays fully functional. Batteries last an estimated 5-7 days under continuous use.

If the power flickers

The control board may freeze. Unplug the adapter from the wall, wait at least 30 seconds, then plug it back in. Wait the same 30 seconds any time you unplug the stove.

Changing the batteries

  1. The battery box is on the right side as you face the stove, below the side panel. Lower it carefully so the cover faces up, without pulling on its wires.
  2. Release the catch at the end and lift the cover off.
  3. Replace the old batteries with new ones.
  4. Put the cover back and re-engage the flange on the screw in the side panel.

Status lights

On the control board at the back, only the blue (programmed) and green (power) lights should be on. Red means the sensor in the firebox (the firebox thermocouple) is disconnected or not working; yellow means the flue collar thermocouple is. Call your Pacific Energy dealer.

warranty.title: Warranty at a glance
warranty.html:
Pacific Energy's warranty covers the original registered purchaser.

Limited lifetime (10 years), parts onlyPorcelain finish, glass (thermal breakage only, not impact), plating, firebox, baffle
3 years comprehensive, parts and laborAny defective part, including blowers, speed controls and thermal switches
Not in lifetime coverageFirebox rails, heat shields
Not warrantedFirebrick, gaskets, ceramic fiber blankets

What can void it

  • Misuse, abuse, improper installation, accident, lack of maintenance or modification
  • Signs of improper use, such as excessive draft, heating too large an area, or contaminated fuel (high sodium, plastics, chemicals)
  • Tampering with the combustion air control, over-firing, or burning salt-water wood or garbage

Porcelain colours may darken when hot and return to their shade when cool.

To make a claim

Contact your dealer with proof of purchase, the purchase date, and the model name and serial number. Register at pacificenergy.net/register; the serial number is on the certification label or the manual cover.

This is a summary. The full terms are in the manual.

specAir.title: Combustion air
specAir.html:
Air comes from the room (through the opening in the ash box enclosure into the firebox intake) or from outside. Outside air is necessary for mobile homes and optional for residential installs; outside or fresh air may be required by local code, so check it or CAN/CSA-B365 first.

Outside air through the floor

Cut a hole behind the ash box enclosure, large enough for 4" metal venting, and run it under the floor per code, from a ventilated crawl space or ducted to the outdoors. Attach the 4" OAIR adapter to the ash box enclosure and connect with 4"(100mm) i.d. flexible metal ducting. Outside, use a 4" hooded inlet or a 90 elbow turned down, with rodent screen; with a well-ventilated crawl space it needn't extend outside.

Outside air from behind

Use a 4"(100mm) wall air intake per its kit; fit the 4" intake adapter over the hole in the rear of the ash box enclosure and connect with flexible metal ducting.

Residential outside air requires securing the unit to the structure so the duct can't dislodge.

Keep the room well ventilated: negative pressure can pull fumes into the living area. In extreme cold with slow burns, an exposed chimney top can ice up and block flue gases.

specMobile.title: Mobile home installation
specMobile.html:
These are in addition to the residential requirements.

  • Listed double-wall connector with a compatible ULC-S629 or UL-103HT listed chimney. Horizontal connector not permitted (rating label, p. 3).
  • Outside air supply must be used (outside air kit).
  • Anchor the stove permanently: hook the leg anchors provided around the bolts in the bottom of the legs and secure them to the floor with 1/4-20 x 2" lag screws.
  • Not in a sleeping room. Not connected to a flue serving another appliance.
  • Maintain the structural integrity of the floor, walls and ceiling/roof.

Clearances are the double-wall values (8" side and back walls, 5" corner); see Clearances to combustibles. A certified installer (NFI, CSIA, WETT or APC) is strongly recommended.

Each drawing value is exactly 3 in. more than a label value; the text doesn't say whether the drawing measures to the connector centreline.

US floor protection: rating label gives G 16 in. front, H 5 in. side, I 0 in. back; Floor Protector section gives 16" front and 8" to the sides of the fuel loading door opening (min. 33" wide x 34 3/8" deep) and its drawing has an unlabeled 3" (75mm) dimension. Canadian values agree (18 / 8 / 8 in.). Also flagged in step 3.
Blower current: '115 volts A.C.-1.1 amps' in Optional Blower (p. 26) vs 'FAN ELECTRICAL RATING: 115V, 60HZ, 1.0 AMP' on the rating label (p. 3).

review.notes: Model split: the manual (100006922, 061026-36) covers 'Alderlea T4 LE2' only and never names the Alderlea T4 Classic LE2 (the only 'Classic' is the Vista Classic LE2 on the shared rating label). Finishes are separated only in the parts list (p. 30): metallic black paint, Majolica brown enamel and ivory enamel part numbers for the top, sides, door crown, ashlip, leg casting and door. Every spec, clearance and procedure is given once, so there are no per-model rows; the catalog describes the Classic as Majolica or Ivory porcelain enamel. The paint-curing section (p. 5) doesn't say whether it applies to enamel finishes. The rating label (p. 3) is shared with the Vista LE2 and Vista Classic LE2; only the Alderlea T4 LE2 rows were used. The label's jumbled two-column text and the p. 3 efficiency table (HHV 75%, LHV 82%, ideal 16 inches, maximum 17 inches) were paired by column position in the layout text. Not transcribed because the text doesn't label them: Figure 1 dimensions (p. 13), the 56" (1.42m) minimum on the venting drawings (pp. 21-22), and the Figure 12/19 connector values (flagged as a conflict instead). Not in the manual, so these catalog values are unverified: heating area, max cordwood BTU output, burn time, firebox volume, weight, view and glass area. Catalog efficiency 75.4% HHV is consistent with the manual's rounded 75%. Unit-clearance mm values differ slightly between the label and the drawings (254 vs 255, 178 vs 180, 203 vs 205, 127 vs 130 mm); the inch values agree. The manual doesn't explain what the control board or motor control does, or the battery type; only what it states is used. Do-not-burn list (p. 6) includes wet, green and unseasoned wood, while p. 8 says that if you feel you must burn wet or unseasoned wood, keep the air open; both are shown in the wood drawer. Internal cross-references are off (p. 14 'Baffle Removal page 11' is p. 12; p. 20 'clearances diagram (See Page 16)' is p. 18 and 'Figure #10, 11, Page 19-20' are Figures 13-14 on pp. 21-22; p. 17 'Figure #7' is Figure 10; p. 22 'Figs. 12-15' are Figures 15-18; p. 29 'Proper Draft' on 'page 8' is p. 9); the guide uses physical pages. Limited lifetime warranty is printed as '(10 years)'. Pages 33-35 are blank. The French label text duplicates the English; nothing French-only was used.
